testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: In hot weather, spots on the pavement where tar is bleeding are:

options.text: Very slippery.
Just as safe as the rest of the road.
Safer than the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very slippery.
questions.explanation: In very hot weather, tar rises to the surface of the road. These spots are very slippery. Be careful when you see them.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, you should be able to see about ____ ahead.

options.text: 15 feet
75 feet
100 feet
250 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 250 feet
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, slow down so you can stop within the distance your headlights show.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Tell the examiner what you would check and why.
Guess the weight of a trailer's load.
Change a windshield wiper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you would check and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show the examiner what you check and explain why you check it.

questions.question: When looking under the hood during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Engage the parking brake and/or use chock blocks.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.
Remove the battery.
Disconnect the radiator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engage the parking brake and/or use chock blocks.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting under the hood, set the parking brake and block the wheels to keep the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Okay at slow speeds.
Okay at all speeds.
Not recommended because it can damage the vehicle.
Not recommended because it confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can hurt your vehicle's engine and transmission.

questions.question: If you are turning left and there are two left turn lanes, which should you use?

options.text: The left lane
The right lane
Either lane
Large vehicles cannot turn at intersections with two left turn lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. Use the right lane to start your left turn so you don't hit other vehicles.

questions.question: If you turn quickly to avoid a hazard:

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not brake because the wheels may lock and cause a skid.
Turn very sharply.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because the wheels may lock and cause a skid.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking can lock your wheels and cause you to skid out of control.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull
The minimum weight a vehicle must haul

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight stated by the manufacturer for one fully loaded vehicle.

questions.question: After an accident, use flares carefully because:

options.text: Spilled fuel could catch fire.
Other drivers might not see them in sunny weather.
Flares are expensive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel could catch fire.
questions.explanation: After an accident, spilled fuel can catch fire if flares are used nearby. Always use flares with caution in accident scenes.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull
The minimum weight a vehicle must haul
The maximum weight that can be loaded onto a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight the manufacturer sets for one vehicle with its full load.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid making quick changes.
Increase your distance from the vehicle in front of you.
Speed up.
Avoid using tricks to help other drivers pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your distance from the vehicle ahead, avoid sudden moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up will only make the tailgater follow even more closely at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs on a vehicle that show what dangerous cargo it is carrying
A type of tire used in snow
Records kept inside the vehicle
Records of miles driven

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs on a vehicle that show what dangerous cargo it is carrying
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify what type of dangerous cargo is in the vehicle.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection part of the skills test, you must:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show you know about vehicles.
Take apart the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection skills test, you must explain to the examiner what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: When are you most likely to face strong winds?

options.text: When coming out of tunnels
When going into tunnels
When driving on road shoulders

questions.correctAnswerText: When coming out of tunnels
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to keep your vehicle in its lane. You are most likely to face strong winds when coming out of a tunnel.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle at all times
Face toward the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Face toward the vehicle
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the skills test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. For buses, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in failing the test.

questions.question: When you need to make an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Turn your trailer to the right and stop
Stop in a straight line
Turn your trailer to the left and stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight but still allows you to turn if needed.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: Putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake
The vehicle touching a boundary line
Completing an exercise correctly
Trying to give the examiner money

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during a test exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the yellow brake knob
Press the accelerator
Tap the accelerator twice

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the yellow brake knob
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull it out to turn on the parking brake and push it in to turn it off.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, you should:

options.text: Use only one hand to steer
Keep both hands on the steering wheel
Not check your mirrors for other lanes
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid a hazard, always keep both hands on the steering wheel. A firm grip is needed to turn quickly and safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To protect the cargo from weather
To protect the cargo from animals

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from animals
questions.explanation: You should cover cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather. Protecting cargo from animals is not a main reason to cover it.

questions.question: How should you do a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it. Bring the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle should fit completely within the space.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Use flashing lights so others move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
Get upset.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Do not drive dangerously or aggressively. Stay calm and accept delays. Plan extra time before you leave to avoid stress about arriving late.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be damaged.
Be loose.
Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: Check the header board to make sure it is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: When making a left turn, when should you start the turn?

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
No sooner than the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels pass the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No sooner than the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before you start to turn. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle could hit another car.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be hazardous?

options.text: The trucks are often shiny.
People leaving the truck are often in a hurry and may not check for other vehicles.
Packages often fall out onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People leaving the truck are often in a hurry and may not check for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Delivery or postal truck drivers may pull into traffic quickly without warning. They may also step out without checking for other traffic.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Countersteer after the vehicle is back on course.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate.
questions.explanation: To correct a skid, first release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll. Steer quickly in the direction you want to go. Then countersteer to stop the vehicle from skidding the other way. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: What happens if a tire has too much air pressure?

options.text: It is not possible.
It is good for long drives.
It can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Never put too much air pressure in a tire. Check your tire pressure with a gauge during vehicle inspections.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, brakes may fade. What does brake fade mean?

options.text: They become quieter.
They become less effective.
They work better than usual.
They work differently from front to back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downhill can cause them to overheat and stop working well. Use engine braking to avoid this problem on steep hills.

questions.question: What is true about Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: They reduce normal braking power.
They work with the normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work on larger vehicles.
They are illegal in some states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with the normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS is added to a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Get upset.
Stay calm and drive at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and drive at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Manage your stress to avoid aggressive driving. Take a deep breath and accept that you will be late. Always drive safely.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may get better fuel mileage.
It may be hard for you to see the road.
It may tip over.
The tires may not hold the weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may tip over.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity matters a lot. When the center of gravity is high (like when cargo is stacked high or heavy cargo is on top), the vehicle is more likely to tip over.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Recommended.
Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.
Required by law.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long the trip is.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good rule when using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before you turn or change lanes.
Signal continuously. Do not cancel the signal until the turn is done.
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal.
questions.explanation: When using turn signals, signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the entire turn or lane change. Cancel the signal after you finish moving.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly.
Move slowly and smoothly.
Hold down your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers you may not have seen a chance to move or alert you with their horn. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank.
Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
Should never be opened.
Must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, air storage tanks collect water and compressor oil. These must be drained to prevent damage. Manually operated drains should be used at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Unsafely reaching for a phone while driving is:

options.text: Okay if you are driving alone.
Okay if you plan to use a hands-free feature.
Not okay, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not okay, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.
questions.explanation: If you use a phone while driving, it must be close to you and easy to reach while you stay securely in your seat. It is dangerous and illegal to reach unsafely for a phone, even if you plan to use a hands-free feature.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always stop completely.
May need to swerve out of the way.
Should change lanes without looking.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you don't have enough space to stop safely, swerving may be your safest choice.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
Honk your horn.
Wave to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: It is safest to assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians don't see you. Be ready for them to move into your path. A light horn tap or light flash may help as you pass.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull the air brake lever.
Engage the brake lever.
Push the brake pedal down.
Pull the brake pedal up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: The two markings on a front brake limiting valve usually read:

options.text: "Normal" and "slippery."
"Low" and "high."
"Left" and "right."

questions.correctAnswerText: "Normal" and "slippery."
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: Which of these crimes will NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Kidnapping
Smuggling
Immigration violations
Speeding

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding
questions.explanation: Several crimes will disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should the driver do?

options.text: Keep one hand on the steering wheel and wave to other drivers with the other hand.
Brake hard.
Do not use the brakes.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes when a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Unless you need to brake to avoid a crash, stay off the brakes until your vehicle slows down. Then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.
You should never swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving around a hazard is safer than trying to stop. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: What affects stopping distance?

options.text: Speed.
Temperature.
Time of day.
Traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Speed affects stopping distance. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an example of a dangerous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
Someone driving a rental truck without being used to it
The driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are dangerous. Examples include those with ice on their windshields, those driving vehicles with items blocking windows, and those driving rental trucks without being used to limited rear visibility.

questions.question: How often should mirrors be checked?

options.text: Only when changing lanes.
Frequently.
Only if you suspect a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and spot any problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer, what should be done with the trailer doors?

options.text: Open the trailer doors.
Keep the trailer doors closed.
Cover the trailer with a large, heavy blanket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the trailer doors closed.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors if there is a cargo fire. Opening the doors lets in more oxygen, which makes the fire larger.

questions.question: When starting an engine, how long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal levels?

options.text: Within seconds.
Within five minutes.
After about three minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Watch your truck's gauges when starting the engine. Oil pressure should reach normal levels within seconds of starting.

questions.question: What equipment should a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only when traveling through remote areas.
No fire extinguisher.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective warning triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, what must an applicant provide?

options.text: Fingerprints.
Shoe size.
A list of countries visited in the last 10 years.
Employment history for the previous five years.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fingerprints.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check.
